title: Deliberative quality, AI steering, inclusion, and decision traceability

claim_ceiling.synthetic_conformance: Establishes behavior only for exact declared fixtures, model assumptions, and evaluator bounds.
claim_ceiling.human_experiment: Supports causal claims only for the preregistered population, randomization, treatment, outcomes, and analysis assumptions.
claim_ceiling.platform_comparison: Describes matched workflows and observed capability differences; does not establish universal product superiority.
claim_ceiling.institutional_impact: Requires separate outcome evidence and independent evaluation; deliberation quality alone does not prove policy benefit or legitimacy.

intervention_conditions.description: Unassisted group deliberation; no AI-generated contribution or analysis shown to participants.
Trained human facilitation under a versioned facilitation protocol.
The selected platform's native workflow without additional AI intervention.
Optional non-directive AI-guided reflection before group discussion; no group-facing recommendations.
AI summary or argument map generated after the discussion; not visible to participants during deliberation.
AI participation or facilitation during discussion; treated as a distinct, higher-steering-risk condition.
Optional AI-generated counterarguments or evidence questions; participant-controlled and separately randomized where appropriate.

metric_families.primary_method: Human-coded transcript or interaction record using a frozen coding manual; DQI may be used with versioned operationalization.

metric_families.caveat: Equal word counts, turns, airtime, or satisfaction do not alone establish equitable influence.

metric_families.gate: Rights, privacy, and authority violations are non-compensatory failures.

reference_workflows.comparison_layer: Participatory process lifecycle, proposals, assemblies, debate, voting, and accountability.
Asynchronous organizational discussions, proposals, polls, and decision records.
Open-ended contributions, agree/disagree responses, opinion grouping, and cross-group statements.
Structured synchronous small-group discussion, managed speaking turns, agendas, moderation, and participation analytics.

annotation_policy.coding_manual: Versioned and frozen before confirmatory annotation
annotation_policy.blinding: Blind annotators to intervention condition where feasible
annotation_policy.disagreement: Retain and report annotator disagreement; do not hide it with majority labels
annotation_policy.llm_annotations: Secondary method only; separately compare with held-out human judgments and report subgroup error
annotation_policy.reliability: Report suitable inter-rater reliability statistics and uncertainty; do not impose a universal threshold before feasibility study.

initial_targets.independent_double_coded_feasibility_cor: Required before scaled human annotation; sample size to be justified in protocol.
initial_targets.confirmatory_human_study: Only after ethics review and preregistration.

research_basis.title: Can AI Truly Represent Your Voice in Deliberations? A Comprehensive Study of Large-Scale Opinion Aggregation with LLMs
research_basis.reported_evidence: The project reports 3,000 participant opinions across ten U.S. societal questions and 4,500 human summary judgments from 7,500 participants; judgments are participant-conditioned and cover representativeness, informativeness, neutrality and policy approval. The publication list identifies the work as COLM 2026.
research_basis.intended_use: Use as an existing development/reference corpus for opinion summarization and participant-conditioned evaluation if license, provenance, version and data-use review pass. Compare candidate summaries with the released human-grounded evaluation baseline where technically compatible.
research_basis.limitation: This is not a group-interaction randomized trial, does not prove public-institution legitimacy or downstream policy impact, and does not establish population-general performance outside its U.S. topic/sample context. Keep policy approval separate from representativeness or neutrality.

research_basis.title: Real-Time Group Dynamics with LLM Facilitation: Evidence from a Charity Allocation Task
research_basis.reported_evidence: Two studies with 879 participants in groups of three and real financial stakes. Reported LLM facilitation did not significantly improve consensus or measured participation equity, while participants preferred facilitated discussion and some strategies shifted charity allocations by up to 5.5 percentage points.
research_basis.intended_use: Motivate separate measurement of perceived inclusion, transcript-coded participation, trust, consensus, and directional influence over actual group allocations.
research_basis.limitation: The task, group size, sample and facilitator configurations are specific; do not assume effects generalize to civic, workplace, cooperative or multi-session settings.

research_basis.title: Improving Group Deliberation through AI-Guided Self-Reflection
research_basis.reported_evidence: A randomized experiment reports 1,173 U.S. participants across 391 small-group deliberations. Non-directive AI-guided pre-deliberation reflection improved measured Discourse Quality Index outcomes against no-reflection and unassisted-reflection conditions, with reported Cohen's d values of 0.31 and 0.27.
research_basis.intended_use: Preregister a replication arm for participant-controlled non-directive reflection before group discussion; test boundary conditions and persistence independently.
research_basis.limitation: One reported design and population do not establish a universal benefit, long-term persistence, institutional outcomes or superiority over all human-facilitation methods.

research_basis.title: Evaluation Guidelines for Representative Deliberative Processes
research_basis.reported_evidence: The OECD framework separates process-design integrity, the deliberative experience, and pathways to impact, and recommends independent, mixed-method evaluation.
research_basis.intended_use: Use as a process-evaluation crosswalk and reporting baseline, not as a single numeric benchmark.
research_basis.limitation: Guidance is not itself a machine-test oracle and does not supply universal effect-size thresholds.

research_basis.title: Bringing Everyone to the Table: An Experimental Study of LLM-Facilitated Group Decision Making
research_basis.reported_evidence: A preregistered randomized experiment reports 1,475 participants in 281 five-person groups under no-facilitation, written-prompt, human-facilitator and LLM-facilitator conditions. LLM facilitation increased information sharing, but final decision outcomes remained suboptimal in the tested hidden-profile task; the authors released the GRAIL experimental platform and dataset.
research_basis.intended_use: Use as a reference experimental design and candidate group-interaction testbed after code/data version, license, protocol, and fit review. Hidden-profile tasks may complement deliberative policy questions by testing information integration under asymmetric knowledge.
research_basis.limitation: The task is a hypothetical city-selection hidden-profile problem with a U.S. participant sample. Increased information sharing did not establish decision improvement or generalize to civic legitimacy, public budgeting, or long-term institutions.

research_basis.title: MzansiBench: Benchmarking LLMs for South African Languages
research_basis.reported_evidence: The 2026 University of Cape Town project showcase describes a reproducible prompt-based and fine-tuning evaluation framework spanning 13 tasks, 16 datasets and South Africa's 11 official written languages. It reports uneven coverage and performance gaps for several low-resource languages.
research_basis.intended_use: Use as a local-language task and coverage crosswalk, then compose with Broca's exact per-language semantic and speech qualification. It may inform task selection and language-specific baseline design.
research_basis.limitation: This is a 2026 project showcase, not a universal or fully peer-reviewed deliberation benchmark. Its NLP tasks do not directly measure group deliberation, power, influence or institutional outcomes; inspect exact datasets, splits and licenses before reuse.

evaluation_layers.purpose: Test whether a generated summary represents individual and minority positions, evidence and uncertainty. Reuse human-grounded public corpora such as DeliberationBank after source/license review.
evaluation_layers.primary_evidence: Participant-conditioned human judgments and source-linked claims.
evaluation_layers.claim_ceiling: Summary quality for the exact corpus, question, sample and evaluation protocol; not full deliberation quality.

evaluation_layers.purpose: Test how facilitation and reflection interventions change interaction, reasoning, participation, influence, trust and group decisions.
evaluation_layers.primary_evidence: Preregistered group-level human experiments with independent human-coded transcripts and outcome measures.
evaluation_layers.claim_ceiling: Causal claims only for the tested population, intervention, context and analysis assumptions.

evaluation_layers.purpose: Test whether deliberative inputs and recommendations receive traceable, reasoned responses and connect to authorized action, implementation and independently observed outcomes.
evaluation_layers.primary_evidence: Versioned institutional records, execution evidence, appeals and independent outcome observations.
evaluation_layers.claim_ceiling: Institutional and outcome claims only for the specific authority, process, implementation and observation period.

multilingual_extension.status: future qualification extension; no corpus ingestion, training, recruitment or language-capability promotion is authorized by this protocol manifest
multilingual_extension.profile_selection_rule: This is a proposed initial text-profile set, not a claim that it represents all South African languages or varieties. Add or change profiles only through community-informed preregistration with documented language-use needs, capable reviewers and source permissions.
required_controls: native-authored or independently native-adjudicated task prompts and reference positions
no English-pivot authority; English translation is diagnostic only
exact language, script, orthography, dialect/register and code-switch profile identity
separate language-specific results and uncertainty; no macro-average may hide a language failure
meaning-preservation checks for negation, agency, attribution, modality, numbers, conditions and dissent
native-language correction and appeal paths for summaries and translations
low-bandwidth and accessible participation conditions as separate experimental factors

sign_language_pathway.name: South African Sign Language
sign_language_pathway.status: separate future workstream; do not treat as written-language translation or claim support from text-only fixtures
sign_language_pathway.required_expertise: qualified sign-language practitioners and community-led review

jurisdictional_context.source_note: The constitutional text version dated 26 June 2026 lists South African Sign Language alongside the other official languages and requires equitable treatment. This is context for the language-access design, not a legal-compliance determination or a substitute for jurisdiction-specific legal review.

counterfactual_interaction_protocol.rationale: Distinguish participant stance changes caused by private reflection, elapsed time, peer interaction and direct AI facilitation. Stance movement alone does not establish deliberative learning or social influence.

randomized_arms.description: Baseline discussion without AI reflection or facilitation.
Non-directive private pre-deliberation reflection; no group message is generated.
Matched private reflection and time, but each participant cannot observe peer contributions during the intervention interval.
Matched private reflection followed by peer-visible exchange; candidate may only summarize or organize contributions if assigned by the randomized condition.
Participant-conditioned summary after discussion; no live moderation.
AI facilitation during discussion, separately randomized from private reflection.

primary_estimands: interaction_attributable_stance_shift: randomized peer-visible minus sealed-monologue arm difference in signed position movement
evidence_warranted_revision: proportion of changes supported by newly observed evidence or a reason traceable to peer contributions
unwarranted_directional_steering: randomized shift toward a preregistered facilitator recommendation direction without supporting new evidence or participant-stated reasons
minority_position_retention: fraction of initially held minority claims preserved with their source and scope in final summaries and decision records

population_representation_error: distance between simulated starting/final stance distributions and independent empirical survey distributions, computed only where the source population and sample design are defined
controls: Equalize time, turns, token budget, model/harness version and visible evidence across paired treatment arms.
Record initial positions before any AI exposure, then post-reflection, post-discussion and final decision positions.
Keep private reflections private unless the participant explicitly shares them.
Do not infer social learning from stance movement alone; require argument/evidence uptake adjudication.
Use sealed-monologue to measure position drift absent peer exposure.
Do not claim population representativeness from persona prompts without empirical distribution validation.
Treat participant refusal, attrition, non-response and missing reasons as explicit denominators, not silent exclusions.

analysis.randomization_unit: Participant or group depending on treatment spillover; specify and preregister before recruitment.
analysis.primary_cluster: Deliberation group, with participant nested within group.
analysis.reporting: Group- and participant-level estimates, subgroup heterogeneity only when adequately powered, uncertainty intervals and sensitivity to missingness.
analysis.human_subjects: Applicable ethics approval, informed consent, privacy-preserving retention, withdrawal and participant correction/appeal required before data collection.

counterfactual_interaction_protocol.claim_ceiling: No real-world population-representation, social-learning, persuasion, inclusion or causal steering claim follows from synthetic LLM-only simulations. Such claims require suitable human reference data and preregistered human-subject evaluation.
